risks.statement: False readiness can start oversized or ambiguous work.
risks.trigger: Any codex-ready issue fails a readiness rule.
risks.response: Remove the label and repair the issue before execution.

risks.statement: A persistence or identity slice can start before its provider foundation is verified.
risks.trigger: A data-isolation or identity-dependent issue is made ready without its provider dependency complete.
risks.response: Add the dependency and execute the provider foundation first.

risks.statement: Linear release membership can drift from the delivery manifest.
risks.trigger: A live release count or issue assignment differs from the generated release plan.
risks.response: Fail the drift gate, repair the assignment, and read back all affected releases.

risks.statement: The same person is the interim owner and reviewer.
risks.trigger: A second active human workspace member becomes available.
risks.response: Split owner and reviewer before qualifying another product issue.

risks.statement: Scheduled Linear drift enforcement depends on a repository secret.
risks.trigger: The scheduled workflow runs without LINEAR_API_KEY.
risks.response: Fail closed and configure the read-only key before treating scheduled drift as operational.

risks.statement: Default-to-R0 classification can pull later-release behavior and its dependency chain into the first release.
risks.trigger: R0 contains behavior that is not required for the defined one-buyer, one-seller defensible-evaluation journey.
risks.response: Use an explicit R0 journey allowlist and keep enhanced behavior in its owning later release unless a smaller source-bound R0 slice exists.

risks.statement: Truncated Linear list responses can make incomplete issue text look authoritative in the delivery snapshot.
risks.trigger: A listed description contains a truncation marker or omits executable fields present only in the full issue.
risks.response: Fetch the full issue before qualification and fail readiness when full text cannot be obtained.
